drafted_from: tools/audio-transcription/tool-rows.json, do-work/audio_transcription.py, read-data/whisper_loops.py, test/test_whisper_loops.py (observed find-loops run)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Transcribe /Recordings/walk.m4a with word times using my ggml model, then find and repair any Whisper loops." It runs audio_transcription.py transcribe, find-loops and repair on your computer.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads recordings and writes transcript JSON files on the person's computer.
instructions: 1. Install whisper-cli (whisper.cpp), ffmpeg and python, and keep one ggml Whisper model file.
2. Say "Transcribe my recording"; the AI reads the tool row with tools:list and runs audio_transcription.py transcribe --audio ... --out ... --model-path ....
3. It runs find-loops --transcript on the result; if a stretch looped it runs repair --transcript ... --audio ... --model-path ... and then find-loops again to show the loops are gone.
4. Run judge --transcript before trusting the transcript; text --transcript ... --out ... writes [m:ss] paragraphs. For a folder use transcribe-many, repair-many and index.

worked_examples.title: A segment that says one sentence five times is found as a 20 second loop
worked_examples.ask: Find the Whisper loops in my transcript /Recordings/walk.json.
worked_examples.given: Observed by running do-work/audio_transcription.py find-loops (read-data/whisper_loops.py, as exercised by tools/audio-transcription/test/test_whisper_loops.py) on a transcript with segment 0 "Hello there." at 0-3 s and segment 1 "Thanks for watching." said five times at 10-30 s; run as: python3 trillion-workshop/tools/audio-transcription/do-work/audio_transcription.py find-loops --transcript /Recordings/walk.json
worked_examples.hands_back: Last line {"result": {"transcripts_with_loops": [{"transcript": "/Recordings/walk.json", "segments": 1, "seconds": 20}], "total_looped_seconds": 20}}; the AI then runs repair for that 20 second stretch and find-loops again.
